paragraphs.text: Multiple critical infrastructure vulnerabilities are under active exploitation, with CISA adding four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and a China-linked group leveraging a VMware vCenter zero-day for administrative access. Simultaneously, cloud hypervisor and supplier breaches demonstrate cross-tenant data exposure and credential compromise risks that bypass traditional perimeter controls. These developments collectively weaken vulnerability management, data protection, and third-party risk assurances across cloud and identity infrastructure.

AI supply chain integrity is also compromised, as three inference providers suffered months of undetected prompt theft despite Zero Data Retention settings, and a widely used cryptographic library contains a critical memory flaw affecting all downstream applications. Control owners should prioritize emergency patching of KEV-listed assets, verify hypervisor isolation in shared environments, review supplier access scopes for cloud and AI services, and confirm cryptographic library versions across the software supply chain.
